paragraphs: I've followed West Alamo closely for a long time, and single-story homes on Sunnybrook with a saltwater pool, a fully updated kitchen with a commercial-grade range, and a private backyard setting don't come along often. When I saw this one come to market in June, I made a note of it immediately. When it came off the market without a sale after 22 days, that's what prompted me to put this packet together.

Twenty-two days is not a disaster, but in West Alamo at $1,998,000, it signals something worth examining. This home has the bones, the updates, and the setting that buyers in this price range are actively looking for. The listing description covered the checklist, but it didn't build a case for why this specific combination of features justifies the number, and it didn't tell the story of what living here actually looks and feels like. At $917 per square foot, a buyer comparing options needs more than a list of improvements. They need to understand what they're getting that they can't find anywhere else on the market right now.

I've put together a focused analysis of what the listing history suggests held this home back, along with a clear picture of where this property stands relative to the current Alamo market. The report includes specific friction points and a realistic plan for what a relaunch would need to look and feel like to get a different result.

If you're already working with a real estate agent toward a new listing, please feel free to set this aside with my compliments. If you're not, I'd welcome a conversation whenever the timing feels right for you.

exec_summary.headline: A Turnkey Single-Story in West Alamo with a Saltwater Pool  -  and a Listing That Didn't Make the Case
exec_summary.p1: 1489 Sunnybrook Rd. is the kind of home Alamo buyers at this price point are genuinely searching for. Single-story living, a 10,608-square-foot lot, a saltwater pool with private landscaping, a fully updated kitchen anchored by a commercial-grade gas range, and smart-home lighting throughout. The primary suite has a thermostatically controlled fireplace and a large walk-in closet. The interior and exterior have both been freshly painted, the flooring is new throughout, and the driveway and fencing have been recently redone. This is a home that has been maintained and upgraded with real care, and it shows in person.
exec_summary.p2: The listing history tells a different story. At $917 per square foot, this home is priced in the middle of the Alamo standard range, which is entirely defensible for everything it offers. But the marketing didn't build that defense. The listing description ran through the upgrade list without connecting those features to a buyer's actual life. The pool, the single-story floor plan, the West Alamo school district, the proximity to both Danville and Walnut Creek  -  each of those deserves its own moment in the narrative, not a sentence in a long paragraph. The home left the market after 22 days without a sale, which means the right buyer was either never reached or never given a compelling enough reason to move.
exec_summary.p3: A relaunch for this property needs to do two things: reach the specific buyer profile that values single-story living, a private pool, and top schools in West Alamo, and present this home with the visual depth and narrative clarity to justify $917 per square foot before that buyer ever schedules a showing.

forensics.title: Friction #1: The Listing Description Checked Boxes Without Telling a Story
forensics.body: The MLS remarks for 1489 Sunnybrook read like a well-organized punch list: new flooring, new pavers, new fencing, epoxy garage floor, Lutron dimmers. Every item is real and every item adds value. But at $1,998,000, buyers aren't scanning a checklist. They're trying to picture their life in a home. The description never placed the reader in that backyard next to the saltwater pool on a summer evening. It never explained why a single-story floor plan matters at this price point in Alamo, or what it means to be minutes from both Danville and Walnut Creek. The home has a genuine story to tell. The listing just never told it.

forensics.title: Friction #2: The Visual Assets Were Never Given the Stage They Deserved
forensics.body: A saltwater pool with irrigated private landscaping on a 10,608-square-foot West Alamo lot is a premium feature that lives or dies on how it's shown. Standard MLS photography, shot from ground level with a wide angle, tends to flatten outdoor spaces, and buyers scrolling at speed on Zillow or Realtor.com can't feel the depth or the privacy that make a backyard like this genuinely special. The same is true of the home's single-story footprint, the updated kitchen, and the overall setting on Sunnybrook. At $917 per square foot, buyers are comparing this home against every other option in the Alamo market, and they're making early judgments online before they ever schedule a showing.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: BrightWork uses Sky Tour aerial videography to show the lot position, backyard setting, and neighborhood context in ways ground photography simply can't replicate, giving buyers a reason to make the drive before they've talked themselves out of it.

forensics.title: Friction #3: The Right Buyer Was Never Actively Sought
forensics.body: At $1,998,000 in West Alamo, the buyer pool is real but selective. This is a price point where buyers have options, they research carefully, and they don't respond to passive MLS distribution the way buyers at lower price points sometimes do. The profile for this specific home, a single-story with a pool, top schools, and turnkey condition, skews toward families with school-age children, professionals relocating from San Francisco or Oakland who want flat living without a condo, and buyers actively comparing Alamo against Danville and Orinda. Those buyers can be found and reached directly. A standard listing strategy waits for them to find the home. That's a meaningful difference when you're 22 days in without an offer.

positioning_table.verdict: At $917/sqft versus a benchmark range of $850-$950/sqft, this home sits near the upper end of that range. At $917 per square foot, this home sits in the middle of the Alamo standard tier, which is the right place for a fully updated single-story with a pool and no HOA in a top-school district. The numbers are defensible, but only if the marketing builds the case for them. The saltwater pool, the lot size, the smart-home systems, and the single-story floor plan together represent a combination that commands attention in this market. The strategy going forward needs to show buyers exactly why this specific package justifies the price, not leave them to figure it out on their own.
